A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the N-(2-pyrilidyl) amides of 1-alkyl-4-hydroxyl-2-quinoline-3-carboxilic acids have a high antiinflammatory activity, and the N-(2-heterocyclic) amides of these compounds, which have a higher lipophilic character, have a higher activity.
the amides of 1-alkyl- and 1-cycloalkyl-4-hydroxycoumarin-3-carboxamide acids, and 1-alkoxycarbonyl- and 1-acyloxyalkyl-4- hydroxycoumarins-3-carboxamides, are promising as antiinflammatory agents.
the N-(2-pyril)amide of ethyl 2-quinolylcarboxylate is the most active compound of the series studied.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amides of 1-methyl- and 1-phenyl-substituted 4-hydroxyquinoline-3-carboxlic acids are the most active antiinflammatory agents among those studied.
N-(2-pyrindyl)amide of ethyl 4-hydroxyquinolone-2-carboxylate is a promising antiinflammatory and analgesic agent.
the amides of 2-pyridinecarboxylic acid with 1-R-quinolone carboxylic acids are more active than the corresponding 2-pyrazine and 2-pyrimidinecarboxylic amides.
